misconceptions.description: Attributing moral responsibility to the AI system itself rather than to the humans whose decisions deployed it
misconceptions.trigger: learner says 'the AI made the wrong choice, the company is not at fault'
misconceptions.feedback: Machines are not moral agents under any major ethical framework. Responsibility distributes across developer, deployer, operator, and user.

misconceptions.description: Treating any nominal human reviewer as satisfying the human-oversight requirement
misconceptions.trigger: learner cites 'a human is in the loop' without testing capacity, time, authority, information
misconceptions.feedback: Meaningful oversight requires all four (capacity, time, authority, information) at the stakes of the decision. Structural rubber-stamping is not oversight.

misconceptions.description: Treating audit trails as optional infrastructure that can be added later
misconceptions.trigger: learner ships a high-stakes system without per-decision logging
misconceptions.feedback: Without audit trails, post-hoc accountability is unverifiable. Logs must be designed in from the start and retained at the relevant timescale.

misconceptions.description: Treating model cards and datasheets as marketing rather than as accountability artifacts
misconceptions.trigger: learner produces a polished feature list under the heading 'model card'
misconceptions.feedback: Model cards (Mitchell et al. 2019) document intended use, known limitations, and disaggregated performance. They discharge the failure-to-warn duty and support deployer fit-for-purpose decisions.
